Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter to Parquet
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly master index and turn it into a local Parquet file of canonical rows.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` scaffold; an SEC User-Agent identity from your partner
      Produces: a working download (identifying User-Agent, ≤3 req/s) and master-index parser for one quarter; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one real archived quarter's master.idx is downloaded and stored locally with its SHA-256; O3 — a Parquet file whose row count equals the index's data lines, with the §4.5 row fields; measured cost of the real run: bytes, elapsed time, peak memory and request count, recorded in the findings file
      Leaves out: source manifest and provenance (Stage 2); fixture validation suite (Stage 2); request budget shared across collectors (Stage 4); versioned generations and pointer (Stage 5); deployment and scheduling (Stages 7–8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Shared commands, raw snapshots and replay
      Objective: Turn Stage 1 into the shared discover/collect/transform/publish commands, with content-addressed raw snapshots, observations and a source manifest.
      Outcomes: O5, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader and parser; Stage 1 findings
      Produces: the `sec-edgar-ingest` CLI with four commands that pass worksets; raw and observation storage per §4.5; the source manifest; golden fixtures for the formats Stage 1 met
      Exit: O5 — quarterly backfill runs through the four commands with no quarterly-only download or parse path; O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and an unchanged hash skips work
      Leaves out: daily discovery (Stage 3); shared request budget (Stage 4); generations and pointer (Stage 5); Azure storage and Table Storage (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes through the shared commands, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2's commands, workset and manifest
      Produces: daily source selection; pending and failed source tracking; `no_new_sources` reporting
      Exit: O2 — from a handoff date, one real daily index is ingested, and a simulated outage across a quarter boundary catches up with no lost pending sources
      Leaves out: scheduled triggers (Stage 8); shared request budget (Stage 4)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: One SEC request budget
      Objective: Put every SEC request from every collector under one lease-held budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 2's collector; Stage 3's daily collector
      Produces: a lease-held collector that backfill, daily and later reconciliation all use
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily collectors never overlap as request issuers, retries count toward the budget, and lease loss stops new requests
      Leaves out: lease on deployed Azure Storage (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind one conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's publish command and observations
      Produces: generations with manifest and change report; the active-pointer contract that readers and reconciliation use
      Exit: O9 — injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer update and after it leave readers seeing only complete generations, and competing publishers lose no update
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate (Stage 6); Table Storage pointer on Azure (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and gate withdrawals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's shared collector; Stage 5's generations and pointer
      Produces: reconciliation source selection; approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — a changed quarterly fixture publishes its additions and field updates as a recorded change; O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays unpublished until an approval names its exact hash, open-quarter absence withdraws nothing, and stale daily replay does not resurrect a withdrawn key
      Leaves out: weekly trigger (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment and configuration
      Objective: Run the shared commands on Azure under ADF, with typed, validated configuration and versioned infrastructure.
      Outcomes: O4, O11
      Consumes: Stages 2–6; the ADR and spec accepted and the §4.8 deployment values recorded (spec §7 step 1)
      Produces: infrastructure as code; pinned image digest and configuration revision; ADF pipelines with triggers disabled; an isolated environment that passed the smoke test
      Exit: O4 — in an isolated environment, ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome, the live smoke test runs one archived quarter and one daily index, and replay with SEC access disabled gives unchanged output; O11 — an invalid configuration is refused before any network request
      Leaves out: production triggers, monitoring alerts and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill, catch up daily ingestion, run reconciliation once, then enable and observe the schedules.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployed environment and release record
      Produces: a published baseline over the approved range; enabled daily and weekly triggers; alerts and runbooks per §4.7 and §8
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline unit is published, or the incomplete range is recorded and approved; O2 — observed scheduled daily runs, each with a durable report; O7 — one observed scheduled reconciliation, with any gated candidate resolved
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
